items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1979-12-07
items.q: when I was playing with the Ureka band... Willie Pajot said... I said, see, Frank Sanders, what I'm playing.

ctx.x: So like a new musician, you know, wouldn't be able to identify her? No, no. Oh, so you know, like he went into the piece Cole. Yeah. Uh-huh. Because I was thinking that, you know, for the most part, that after they heard the first little bit, they could fake it.

Well, probably some of them can, that heard it enough. But if they never heard it, well they have to read the music. See? Because when I was playing with the Ureka band, they had a number that I loved, number 51. I don't know the name. But I know it's number 51. And Willie Pajot said, oh, that's a beautiful part. I said, see, Frank Sanders, what I'm playing. They said, but I never heard nobody playing before. I said, because they weren't reading the music. If they were playing these notes, you'd have heard it. I…
I believe some time ago you said that the, you know, from what I read in the jazz archives, the interview in jazz archives, you said that the parade music had actually gotten worse.
